recipes.name: Quick Eggplant Parmesan
ingredients_raw: 1 small eggplant, cut into 3/4 inch thick slices
0.25 cup vegetable oil, or as needed

steps.text: Beat together egg and water in a small bowl. Place bread crumbs in a shallow dish.
Dip eggplant slices in egg mixture, then press in bread crumbs to coat.

Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add eggplant slices to hot oil, then reduce heat to medium. Cook until golden brown and tender, 3 to 4 minutes per side. Sprinkle mozzarella cheese over eggplant during the last minute of cooking to melt.
While eggplant is cooking, combine spaghetti sauce and red pepper flakes in a microwave-safe measuring cup. Cover with plastic wrap and cook on high until heated through, about 2 minutes.
Top fried eggplant slices with sauce and Parmesan cheese to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Quick Eggplant Parmesan
raw_recipe.description: This quick eggplant recipe uses the microwave and stovetop to make a simple and tasty Italian meal with jarred spaghetti sauce in just 15 minutes.

review.reviewBody: Fabulous recipe. After I cooked the eggplant I put them in a baking dish, sprinkled with mozzarella, parmesan and spooned jarred sauce and place the tray in the oven until the cheese melted. Easy and very good.

Very good. Changed a little but feel I kept the recipe intact. Once I'd browned the eggplant finished cooking in 350 degree oven. After 15 min. Added a spoon of sauce over each piece, a small handful of mozzarella. And a sprinkle of parm. Turned off oven and left for 10 min. Residual heat of oven warmed the sauce and melted the cheese. Able to finish rest of meal while in oven. Served on a bed of a wild rice blend. Also fruit and a salad.

Lots of changes made: For 4 servings. -preparation in the oven, instead of skillet, - 1 glass of vegetarian Bolognese sauce, - 1 quart of tomato passata, - double the mozzarella, - double the parmesan, - less bread crumbs necessary, probably half to 2/3, - 2 normal eggs vs. two large eggs, - 2 medium to large size eggplants, - more olive oil, Time in the oven: -30 minutes for the eggplant, - 20 minutes with the sauce, - just short of 30 minutes with the mozzarella and parmesan cheese on top.

I baked the slices at 375 for about 30 min, turning half way through. Added cheese the last five minutes. Used 1/2 C sauce which I added before serving. Also used Panko crumbs, rather than bread crumbs. Turned out very crisp & hubs enjoyed every bite!

I didn't know I liked eggplant until I tried this recipe! Quick to fix and very tasty for a side dish or meatless main dish. I dipped the eggplant in flour before the egg wash and patted it firmly into the crumb mixture (I used half seasoned bread crumbs and half Panko to total 1-1/2 cups). I had to add a little more water to stretch the egg wash. I also used more sauce because we like it that way. Thank you for sharing this wonderful dish!

I used a large eggplant, sliced 1/2" , cooked in nonstick pan. Then in the baking dish, some sauce, the egg plant layered, the rest of the sauce topped with mozzarella cheese. baked while some spagetti cooked. then broiled to brown the cheese....delicious!
(and as someone else mentioned, salt the slices and let sit while mixing the egg mixture, pat the moisture off and the bitterness is greatly reduced)

I made this exactly as described (almost). I also used the recommendation from others to sweat the eggplant for an hour with a bit of salt. Quite a bit of moisture came out. Instead of marinara sauce, I used the last bit of pizza sauce that was in the fridge. I added a little sugar to it to sweeten it up some. I was pleased with the texture of the finished product. The taste was good, too.

Yummy recipe! Made great leftovers, too! To cut some of the fat, I fried the eggplant in a nonstick skillet with only 1 tsp. of olive oil and used reduced-fat (Kraft 2 percent) mozzarella. Served it over whole grain penne. YUM!
I used Barilla bottled sauce but overall found this dish to be kind of salty (even though I looked for the lowest sodium breadcrumbs I could find), so next time I would omit the salt when boiling the penne to make up for it.

This recipe is quick and easy and very good. I didn't have the red pepper flakes, and besides leaving that out and salting the eggplant slices to draw out the moisture, I followed the recipe as written. I served it with a side of pasta and a fresh salad.

I made these on a night when our Son was home from College and his Dad wanted to order Pizza -- so I made this for our dinner as well. I doubled the recipe because our Son is a big eater.

I also added Onion Powder, Garlic Salt and Black Pepper to the Bread Crumbs. I popped it into the oven for about 10 minutes to melt the cheese and heat it up a little. 

I was AMAZED to see both my Husband and Son getting seconds -- they usually get disappointed when I bring Vegetables to the table!

They next time I made them -- I made both the Eggplant and added some Zucchini (cooked the same way). Hubby did a repeat and ate tons of both. It's a Keeper Recipe :)

Im not the best cook for sure but my family loved this when i made it !!! I added a couple steps to the orginal reciepe. First I laid the eggplant slice's out and sprinkled salt over them and let them sit for a couple minitues, then used paper towels to soak up the water that the salt pulled out. Then I added flour to the slices after the first batch (bread crumb stuck better) before putting them in the egg batter. I also put them in a browine pan when i added the sauce and broiled them to melt to cheese. Everything came out Faboulous!!
An easier version of an old favorite! Even my kids, who are not the biggest fans of eggplant, liked it! I would make this again for sure!

What an interesting Parmesan. This was very easy to make, and it works best with a small eggplant. The smaller, the better it came out really good. I wasn’t sure about not dipping the eggplant and flour before the egg but it worked perfectly. The breading stayed on it real nice. I’m sure this would work equally as well with zucchini too. Anything to use up those summer vegetables. I messed up and I put the sauce on before the cheese, but it still came out perfect. I plan on making this one again. it is so quick.

I pretty much followed the recipe. I added more sauce and will probably add more crushed red pepper flakes the next time I make it. I let my friend try it and he loved it. I'll definitely make this again.
Easy and everyone loved it! Thank you

I had never had eggplant parmesan. I am staying in the Fisher house at the Veterans hospital with my dad and they were selling eggplant out in front of the hospital. Fisher house has some items in the pantry like cheese, spaghetti sauce, eggs, hot pepper flakes, parmesan cheese and croutons so I made this dish. I used meunster cheese because that's all I had. This exceeded my expectations. It's the best eggplant dish I have ever had. I added extra hot pepper flakes because I like it like that but omg delicious. My husband and kids don't like eggplant because I usually stir fry it but I was bragging how good this was on the phone to them. When I get home I am making it for them and I know they're gonna love it. 5 stars especially for not having to use the oven.
Awesome recipe!! I definitely recommend it, it’s a perfect vegetarian dinner
Very easy to make and it was light and tasty. Not to heavy as I find some eggplant recipes. Nice quick dinner with pasta and a salad.
Loved this - my family asked for it again.
This was very tasty. I had some leftover bread crumbs so I used to cook sliced red pepper the same way. That was really tasty too. Nice easy recipe. Yummy!
